title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional backoff to prevent thrashing during failover
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: during last week's partial regional outage we observed the SLO enforcer's backoff/CB logic thrashing: regions would rapidly flip between healthy/unhealthy, triggering repeated regional failovers and aggressive load-shedding. This PR stabilizes the enforcer by adding deterministic backoff ordering, jitter caps, and an explicit per-region cooldown window so we avoid cascading failovers and oscillation.

Summary of changes: implemented ordered backoff queue so backoff decisions are applied in the same causal order they were observed; added a configurable max-jitter and exponential cap to prevent wide variance in retry timing; introduced a per-region cooldown label (region_cooldown_until) enforced by the enforcer so a region that was recently failed over will not be re-selected until the cooldown expires; tightened concurrent backoff updates by switching the region state map to use a compare-and-swap update path; added integration tests that simulate multi-region thrash and a deterministic fake-clock for test stability.

Testing / CI: new unit and integration tests included. Ran canary on staging and observed no oscillation under a replay of the incident load. Integration test initially failed due to reliance on real timers; switched tests to fake clock and fixed flakiness.

Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, health-check canary (10% traffic) for 1 hour, increase to 100% if no oscillation. Feature flag slo.enforcer.regional_cooldown is off by default and will be enabled during canary.

Notes: ties to Linear ENG-2847 and SRE post-incident SUP-1998. This is a hotfix candidate and should be cherry-picked to the latest release/* branch if approved for emergency patching.
